details: Bitcoin experienced a significant pullback from its recent high of $87,000, dropping below $81,000 and settling around $82,000-$83,000. This decline was accompanied by over $1 billion in liquidations, predominantly affecting leveraged long positions, and nearly $1 billion in ETF outflows over two days. Macroeconomic factors like rising interest rates, inflation concerns, and escalating Middle East tensions contributed to the broader crypto market pressure.
title: Bitcoin Retreats to $82K Amid $1B Liquidations & ETF Outflows

details: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) has set a January 8, 2027, deadline for MiCA-authorized crypto firms to address client exposure to non-compliant stablecoins, effectively restricting services for such tokens. Separately, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) proposed a new federal regulatory framework for leveraged retail crypto transactions, intending to establish "Crypto Asset Markets" (CAMs) as a subcategory of designated contract markets.
title: EU Sets Stablecoin Deadline, CFTC Proposes New Crypto Trading Rules

details: Russia's banking giant Sberbank has commenced testing cryptocurrency transactions, including Bitcoin, Ether, and USDT, within its banking application, with a target of broader customer access by December 1, pending regulatory approval from the Bank of Russia. Separately, the Sui token saw a short-term price increase following its integration with Samsung Wallet.
title: Sberbank Tests Crypto Trading; Samsung Wallet Boosts Sui

details: Pyth Network's PYTH token surged over 10% after its DAO proposed allocating 100% of product revenue for additional token buybacks, coinciding with an 86.5% quarter-over-quarter revenue growth in Q3. Other altcoins also saw significant gains: Jupiter's JUP rose 4.89% after its Lend protocol surpassed Kamino in Total Value Locked (TVL), Aptos (APT) jumped 12% following a tokenomics overhaul, and XDC Network gained 11.15% due to its Brazil tokenization program expansion.
title: Pyth Network Surges on Buyback Plan; Altcoins See Strong Gains

details: The CME has launched a new "Emerging Crypto Index" designed to track 10 altcoins, with BNB, XRP, Solana, and Hyperliquid dominating approximately 93% of its total weight. Dogecoin was explicitly excluded as a meme coin, while Cardano, Litecoin, and Monero were also removed without clearly stated reasons. This index aligns with the CFTC's recent recognition of XRP and Stellar as digital commodities.
title: CME Debuts Emerging Crypto Index, Focuses on BNB, XRP, SOL

details: Thailand has finalized the regulatory framework that will allow for the introduction of Bitcoin and Ethereum Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) in the country. These new crypto investment products are expected to become available for trading starting from October 16.
title: Thailand Approves Bitcoin & Ethereum ETFs Launching Oct 16
